title: Top 5 ChatGPT Plugins for Presentations in 2026
summary: Compare five ChatGPT plugins for presentations, including Julius, Canva, Gamma, Genspark, and Figma. Find the right workflow for your next slide deck.
body_markdown:
*From messy materials to a presentation your audience can use.*


The right ChatGPT presentation plugin depends on your starting material: a spreadsheet, a product launch outline, or a deck your design team already owns.


Our five picks are **Julius AI, Canva, Gamma, Genspark AI Slides, and Figma** . Julius is our first choice for turning source material into an editable deck. The other tools offer useful options for branding, content repurposing, topic-based slides, and collaborative design.


[Open Julius: PowerPoint & Slides in ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6ad6cbda4b1c81918413a835814d9abd) .


Here, “plugins” means tools connected to ChatGPT, also called apps or connectors. We distinguish their ChatGPT functionality from features in the provider's own workspace.


*Published by Julius AI. Picks reflect documented features. Reviewed October 16, 2026.*


## The best ChatGPT plugins for presentations at a glance


**Plugin** **Our recommended use** **Main consideration**


Julius: PowerPoint & Slides Editable PPTX decks from outlines, documents, and supplied branding Revise supported elements through Julius or continue in PowerPoint


Canva Branded presentations and visual content Connect the correct Canva account and Brand Kit


Gamma Turning an outline or conversation into a presentation Check credits and available editing functions


Genspark AI Slides Creating slides from a topic or brief Genspark's downloadable exports require a paid plan


Figma Decks that a design team will refine together Uploaded assets may need to be added in Figma


## 1. Julius: PowerPoint & Slides


**Best for creating and revising an editable PowerPoint from your source material.**


[Julius: PowerPoint & Slides](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6ad6cbda4b1c81918413a835814d9abd) is the dedicated presentation plugin. You can give it a prompt, outline, notes, Word document, or supported text-based PDF and ask for a real .pptx file with editable text and supported slide elements.


The useful part is being able to define the deck around the meeting. Tell Julius who will see it, what decision you want them to make, and which facts must appear. You can request slide titles, concise talking points, tables, charts, and speaker notes, then refine the structure or individual slides.


For a branded deck, supply the logo, colors, fonts, and layout references you want it to follow. If you are starting from a PDF, treat the task as turning the content into a presentation. It is not a promise to reproduce every PDF page exactly.


**Example prompt:**


> Use Julius: PowerPoint & Slides to turn this project brief into an eight-slide PowerPoint for a leadership review. Open with the decision we need, show the supporting evidence, then cover risks and next steps. Use the attached logo and brand colors. Save an editable PPTX with speaker notes and flag any missing facts.


After the first draft, ask for a specific revision: shorten slide 3, move the recommendation forward, or replace a dense paragraph with a comparison table. Open the downloaded file and check the figures, slide order, font substitutions, and layout before presenting.


If you are exploring the dedicated web workspace, see the[Julius AI presentation maker](https://julius.ai/home/ai-presentation-maker) . For a data-led deck, our guide to[turning Excel data into PowerPoint slides](https://julius.ai/home/excel-to-powerpoint) covers that starting point.


**Keep in mind:** Support for an existing deck depends on its features. The plugin listing establishes PPTX creation and supported edits; it does not promise native Google Slides synchronization or lossless preservation of every animation and embedded object.


## 2. Canva: Best for branded presentations and visual content


Canva is a sensible choice when you already have the story and want to shape its visual identity.


The[Canva app in ChatGPT](https://www.canva.com/newsroom/news/deep-research-integration-mcp-server/) can create, preview, and edit designs within the conversation. Canva also documents Brand Kit support, so available brand fonts, colors, and voice can inform what gets generated. You can ask for wording changes across a design and continue refining it in Canva.


Consider it for sales decks, course materials, and campaign presentations, especially when your team already maintains its visual assets in Canva.


**Example prompt:**


> Canva, turn this outline into an eight-slide sales presentation using our Brand Kit. Keep each slide focused on one idea, use short headlines, and include a clear next step on the final slide.


**Keep in mind:** Canva's[presentation product](https://www.canva.com/presentations/) supports outputs including PowerPoint and PDF, but choose your final format early. Inspect the exported version if the presentation will be delivered outside Canva. Account features and available brand assets also affect the workflow.


## 3. Gamma: Best for turning a conversation or outline into a deck


Gamma is a useful option when your starting material is mostly text: a strategy memo, a rough outline, or a conversation that has finally clarified your argument.


[Connect Gamma to ChatGPT](https://gamma.app/integrations) to turn an outline or conversation into a deck. You can[set the tone, layout, images, and theme](https://help.gamma.app/en/articles/13943863-how-do-i-use-gamma-with-outbound-connectors-and-integrations) , and edit existing Gamma content you have permission to change.


Consider Gamma for internal proposals and repurposing written reports. Agree on the message in conversation, then specify the presentation's audience and length.


**Example prompt:**


> Gamma, turn the approved proposal above into an eight-slide presentation for our operations team. Start with the decision we need, compare the two options, and end with a rollout plan. Use a restrained visual style and keep the wording concise.


**Keep in mind:** Connector use consumes Gamma credits. Available editing functions depend on the connected account and app version; open the deck in Gamma for changes the connection cannot make. See[Gamma's current connection guide](https://developers.gamma.app/mcp/gamma-mcp-server) .


For a closer look at the editor and export tradeoffs, read[our Gamma review](https://julius.ai/articles/gamma-reviews) .


## 4. Genspark AI Slides: Best for presentations that begin with a topic


[Genspark AI Slides has a dedicated ChatGPT listing](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/genspark-ai-slides) for generating presentations from a topic or supplied content.


Consider it when your brief begins with “create a presentation about…” and you want an initial deck to respond to. Include the audience, scope, and intended takeaway in your brief.


The broader[Genspark AI Slides workspace](https://www.genspark.ai/helpcenter/ai-slides) documents research, file imports, slide editing, speaker notes, and exports to PDF, PPTX, and Google Slides. Those are features of Genspark's workspace; the ChatGPT listing itself makes the narrower promise of presentation generation.


**Example prompt:**


> Genspark AI Slides, create a six-slide introduction to customer retention for new account managers. Explain the main concepts, include a clearly labeled hypothetical customer example, and finish with questions the team can discuss.


**Keep in mind:** Genspark currently requires a paid plan to download presentations. Its free plan can present in the browser and share a live link. Check that distinction before choosing it for a deadline that requires a PowerPoint attachment.


## 5. Figma: Best for presentations a design team will refine together


The Figma connection includes **Figma Slides** , so it belongs on a presentation shortlist alongside dedicated slide generators.


Figma's[ChatGPT documentation](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/35326636109975-Use-ChatGPT-with-Figma) explains that ChatGPT turns a prompt into an objective, outline, and style notes, which Figma uses to create a presentation. You can open the result in Figma Slides to keep working on it.


The appeal is strongest for teams already working in Figma. Its[official launch walkthrough](https://www.figma.com/blog/slides-buzz-figma-app-in-chatgpt/) shows teams refining decks, replacing images, and adjusting typography and colors together. Consider it for design reviews, product narratives, and portfolios.


**Example prompt:**


> Figma, create a seven-slide product roadmap presentation from these notes. Use a simple visual hierarchy, distinguish committed work from ideas under consideration, and leave clear spaces for product screenshots we will add later.


**Keep in mind:** Figma says uploaded images and PDFs can inform the prompt, but their contents may not always be embedded in the generated deck. Its help page also lists regional availability and beta usage limits, so check access before planning around it.


## How to get a useful first draft


Start from the provider's ChatGPT listing or connection instructions, connect the account when prompted, and name the tool in your request.[Canva](https://www.canva.com/newsroom/news/deep-research-integration-mcp-server/) and[Figma](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/35326636109975-Use-ChatGPT-with-Figma) both document this direct prompting approach.


Before generating the deck, provide four things: the audience, the decision or lesson, the source material, and the desired length. If you already have a template or approved outline, include it in the brief.


Review the argument before the cosmetic details. Does each slide support your purpose? Are the numbers traceable? Does the final slide explain what happens next? Then refine the design and inspect the final output.


## Frequently asked questions


### Which ChatGPT plugin is best for PowerPoint presentations?


Julius is our recommendation for decks built from data or source files. It combines analysis and slide creation with editable PowerPoint output. Consider Canva for visual branding or Figma Slides when your team finishes presentations in Figma. For the full workflow, see our guide to[making a PowerPoint with ChatGPT](https://julius.ai/articles/can-chat-gpt-make-a-powerpoint) .


### Can I turn Excel data into slides with a ChatGPT plugin?


Julius supports a workflow that analyzes Excel or CSV files and turns the results into charts and presentation slides. Ask it to explain its calculations before generating the deck, especially when the workbook contains multiple tabs or conflicting summaries.


### Are these presentation plugins free?


Generation credits, account features, and export access vary. Genspark, for example, requires a paid plan for downloads. Check the provider's terms for your intended workflow and final file format.


### Do I have to finish the presentation inside ChatGPT?


No. Several of these workflows lead into the provider's editor or an exported presentation. Choose based on where you want to review, collaborate, and make final changes.
